tools.name: heartbeat
tools.description: Check that the Chroma server is alive and get its nanosecond heartbeat counter

tools.name: version
tools.description: Get the Chroma server version string

tools.name: pre_flight_checks
tools.description: Get the Chroma server's client limits, including the maximum batch size it will accept

tools.name: identity
tools.description: Get the identity the stored credential resolves to on this Chroma server: user id, tenant and the databases it may reach

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List the collections in one Chroma tenant and database, with each collection's id, name and vector dimension

tenant.description: Tenant name. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_tenant

database.description: Database name inside the tenant. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_database

offset.description: Number of collections to skip before returning results

tools.name: count_collections
tools.description: Count the collections in one Chroma tenant and database without listing them

tenant.description: Tenant name. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_tenant

database.description: Database name inside the tenant. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_database

tools.name: get_collection
tools.description: Get one Chroma collection's id, name, vector dimension, metadata and configuration by name or id

tenant.description: Tenant name. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_tenant

database.description: Database name inside the tenant. A fresh Chroma server has exactly one: default_database

collection.description: Collection name, or the collection id (UUID) as returned by list_collections

needs_review: The vault marks api_key optional (a Chroma started without an auth provider needs no key) but this spec keeps it in requiredFields as scaffolded, because the bearer template cannot render without it. A fresh unauthenticated container IGNORES the Authorization header, so the live harness can store any placeholder value; a server that DOES enforce auth needs the real token

Chroma's token auth provider can be configured to read the token from AUTHORIZATION as a bearer (what this spec sends, and what the vault entry's testHeaders sends) or from the X_CHROMA_TOKEN header instead. The scaffolded bearer form is kept; an instance configured for X_CHROMA_TOKEN needs auth.type 'header' with that header name, which is a per-deployment fact no spec can decide

Path shape: every collection route in the v2 API is scoped by tenant and database, verbatim '/api/v2/tenants/{tenant}/databases/{database}/collections'. That shape is taken from the v2 REST surface the server publishes itself at GET /openapi.json and from the v1-to-v2 migration guidance that moved the old flat '/api/v1/collections' under the tenant/database scope. The exact docs.trychroma.com anchor in tools_source is UNVERIFIED blind; the live harness against a fresh container is what proves the shape

The fresh-instance tenant and database names are default_tenant and default_database. They are encoded as _probe defaults, not as spec defaults, because the runtime has no default-value mechanism: tenant and database are therefore REQUIRED inputs on every scoped tool so a missing value fails loudly rather than rendering an empty path segment

version, pre_flight_checks, count_collections and count_records answer with bare JSON scalars (a string for version, a number for the counts) rather than objects, so those tools carry truncate with NO pick: a dotted pick cannot address a scalar payload. pre_flight_checks is left unpicked for the same reason plus version drift in its field set

get_collection's v2 path parameter is documented as a collection id, and Chroma's own clients resolve a NAME through the same route. The _probe uses the name quoxproof-live on that basis. If the live harness 404s on the name, the tool needs an explicit id lookup via list_collections first and this note is the reason why

limit and offset on list_collections and list_databases are the parameters Chroma's own admin and client APIs expose for those two calls. Both are clamped (default 20, max 100) and offset is dropped when absent. Unproven blind: an older server that does not know one of them could reject the request rather than ignore it
The _probe collection name is quoxproof-live, which the live provisioner creates. On an instance without it, get_collection and count_records answer 404

Chroma is customer-hosted, so base_url comes from the base_url credential and nothing here is provable against a vendor-run endpoint. Every tool is GET-only and the whole spec stays unproven until the live harness runs it against a real ephemeral container

list_databases dropped 2026-09-12: live proof vs chromadb/chroma:0.5.23 returned 405 Method Not Allowed on GET. count_records dropped: the path param is a collection UUID, not a name (400 InvalidUUID 'Could not parse quoxproof-live as a UUID'); reinstate as collection_id-typed input when chained-call inputs are provable.
